paragraphs: Here's what I love about this one, friend. Jesus gives the Twelve a job, and then He gives them almost nothing to do it with. No bread, no bag, no money in their belts, just a staff and sandals (Mark 6:8-9). The power was never in the packing list, because the authority came from Jesus (Mark 6:7).

So if you've ever felt like you don't have enough to do what God put in front of you, this is for YOU. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer feeling like a worn-out stamper with nothing to offer. Then the One who sent the angel to call me out of that drawer handed me a bakery and a job. What Jesus gave the Twelve was His authority, and that's worth remembering when your own hands feel empty (Mark 6:7).

And notice that He never promises it'll all go smoothly. He tells them some people will not welcome them or listen (Mark 6:11). Their job was to go, to preach that the people should repent, and to keep on going (Mark 6:12). That takes a lot of weight off your shoulders, baker, because you're asked to be faithful, and the results aren't yours to carry.
